title: Slice = delivery boundary, Task = execution boundary, one delivery PR per Slice
problem: Issue #282 asked whether one Task maps 1:1 to one Slice. The control plane treated the Task as the unit that owns a PR and completes, and Task.slice was a free-text label, so one Slice could be delivered through several PRs and milestone progress could not be counted per Slice.

options.summary: Slice = delivery unit, Task = execution unit, PR = Slice delivery unit: every Slice produces exactly one delivery PR; a Slice may hold one or many Tasks on different workers, and their commits are reconciled into that single PR
One Task = one Slice = one PR (1:1:1)
Keep one PR per Task and group PRs under a Slice label

rationale: Owner instruction (2026-09-25), recorded as the final answer to #282. Rule: Slice = delivery boundary, Task = execution boundary, PR = Slice delivery boundary. Invariant: every Slice produces exactly one delivery PR; separate task commits are reconciled into it, and tasks of a Slice never deliver their own PR to main. A Slice is COMPLETE only when all eight gate points hold: (1) every task of the Slice is done; (2) the Slice acceptance criteria are met; (3) exactly one delivery PR exists; (4) the PR's exact-head CI/gates passed; (5) the PR is merged to main; (6) main is re-verified; (7) evidence is recorded; (8) the milestone register is updated. Enforced by the control plane: Slice object and state machine (OPEN -> DELIVERING -> MERGING -> VERIFYING -> COMPLETED), P-program and future-program tasks require a registered OPEN Slice, MQ_ADMIT rejects task-level PRs for slice tasks and admits one Manager-owned delivery item per Slice, a merged Slice delivery can never be followed by a second PR (a rejected unmerged PR reopens the Slice and is recorded), SLICE_COMPLETE checks the eight points in order and completes every task with the Slice. GOVERNANCE work is outside milestone slicing and stays one task = one PR (DEC-0011). Milestone accounting becomes Milestone -> Slices -> one PR each.
